result.summary: The image shows a residential intersection with a high-visibility marked crosswalk and curb ramps. While basic pedestrian infrastructure is present, the intersection lacks pedestrian signals and has parked vehicles that may obstruct sightlines near the crossing.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection on the right side of the image may block the view between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway, adjacent to the crosswalk area

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: The intersection is controlled by a traffic light but lacks dedicated pedestrian signal heads to indicate when it is safe to cross.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve sightlines for both pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear guidance on crossing intervals.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to reduce crossing distance and increase pedestrian visibility.

result.summary: The intersection is equipped with sidewalks and ADA-compliant curb ramps with tactile paving, providing a basic level of accessibility. However, the environment lacks dedicated pedestrian signals and features significant sightline obstructions due to a stone wall and mature trees at the corner.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated walk/don't-walk signals are visible, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicle traffic lights which may not provide adequate clearance time.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: A stone retaining wall and large tree trunks at the corner block the view between pedestrians waiting to cross and drivers approaching the intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: The corner area between the two sidewalks

interventions.title: Install Pedestrian Signal Heads
interventions.description: Add countdown pedestrian signals to provide clear right-of-way and timing information for people crossing.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street lined with multi-story apartment buildings and mature trees. While sidewalks are present, the intersection lacks basic pedestrian safety infrastructure such as marked crosswalks, signals, or curb extensions.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: The lack of marked crosswalks at the intersection forces pedestrians to cross without a designated space or clear priority.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb line block sight lines between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right-hand curb line where cars are parked

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian paths and increase driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight past parked cars.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the intersection to improve visibility for all road users.

result.summary: The image shows a signalized intersection in a residential area with multi-story apartment buildings. Pedestrian infrastructure includes marked zebra crosswalks, sidewalks, and pedestrian signals, though the pavement within the intersection is visibly degraded.

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: Cracking and uneven asphalt in the intersection can cause tripping or affect vehicle handling.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and center of the intersection

hazards.name: Wide Turning Radii
hazards.description: The intersection corners appear wide, which may encourage higher vehicle turning speeds.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to reduce crossing distance and slow turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Pavement Resurfacing
interventions.description: Repair the cracked and uneven asphalt to improve safety for all users.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Program traffic signals to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light.
